scope: Artificial variable-mass, nonproportional-damping known-chart test from material B; not a physical catheter or KAM certificate.
units: All synthetic coordinates, time and matrices are dimensionless declared mathematical test values.
mechanical_model: M(q)=DQ^T M0 DQ; C(q)=DQ^T C DQ; V(q)=Q^T stiffness Q/2; H_q includes every derivative of M(q)^(-1)
chart: chi_t=T(t)*xi with real principal T=(K0^-1 K_y)^(1/2); Tdot by Sylvester; midpoint in transformed field L(t)=Tdot*T^-1+T*A*T^-1

control_comparison.reference: same exact controlled target for both groups
control_comparison.input_assumptions: Ideal, unrestricted, fully actuated two-coordinate generalized force; no learned coefficients, magnetic decoder, measurement noise or saturation.
control_comparison.scope: Confirms a structure can be rebuilt for a closed loop that still has nonproportional drag; not a catheter control-performance result.

error_definitions.solves: Infinity residual of ordinary nonlinear increment, chart linear midpoint increment and inverse xi equation reported separately

limitations: Known nonlinear conjugacy and explicit matrix-exponential K are essential to this test, not an efficient construction for arbitrary f.
Required chart preparation is included in cold cost. Cached warm cost is disclosed separately and cannot establish a universal speed advantage.
No proportional weighted formula or autonomous Central4 is assigned to this general nonautonomous chart problem.
Finite-difference tangent checks and floating-point defects are implementation diagnostics, not interval enclosures or exact arithmetic certificates.

provenance.parameter_policy: Material A is the sole physical baseline. B's display-precision old-v10 values are not loaded.
provenance.structure_policy: Ideal implicit/conjugated tangents evaluated at floating-point states; no assertion that finite Newton code is exactly structure preserving.
